title: Onion Prices Surge Nearly 50 Percent as India Revives Kanda Express Rail Service
excerpt: With retail onion prices crossing Rs 50 per kg in several cities, the Indian government is deploying special rail shipments and releasing buffer stocks ahead of the festive season.
body:
• India's retail onion prices have surged to Rs 34-50 per kg across major cities, rising over 22 percent year-on-year, with wholesale prices jumping more than 30 percent in a single month.
  • The Centre is reviving its Kanda Express — special rail shipments carrying up to 1,700 tonnes of onions per train from Nashik to consumption centres — to stabilize prices ahead of the festive season.
  • The government has set a target to procure 2 lakh tonnes of onions for buffer stocks under the Price Stabilisation Fund and raised the procurement price to Rs 2,125 per quintal.
  • Fresh kharif onions are not expected until November, leaving stored rabi stocks as the only supply bridge during the politically sensitive festive months.

Prices Cross the Pain Threshold

Onion prices across India have breached levels that historically trigger government intervention. The all-India average retail price reached Rs 34.51 per kg as of mid-July 2026, a 22.2 percent increase from Rs 28.25 a year earlier and a 26 percent jump from the previous month, according to data from the Department of Consumer Affairs.

In several local markets, prices have already crossed Rs 50 per kg. Delhi is at Rs 43 (up from Rs 33 a year ago), Chennai at Rs 40 (from Rs 32), and Mumbai at Rs 37, according to the department's price monitoring data reported by Outlook Business. Wholesale markets have recorded even steeper hikes, with the all-India average climbing to Rs 2,716 per quintal — a 30.3 percent monthly increase.

The price rally is hitting household budgets hard. Crisil Intelligence's Roti Rice Report found that the cost of a vegetarian thali rose 5 percent year-on-year in June, driven primarily by onions. Non-vegetarian thali costs climbed 6 percent over the same period.

Enter the Kanda Express

To combat the surge, the Centre is deploying its tried-and-tested Kanda Express — dedicated rail shipments that transport government-stockpiled onions from Nashik, Maharashtra's onion-growing hub, directly to high-demand cities. Each train can carry approximately 1,700 tonnes, the equivalent of 56 truckloads, at roughly half the cost of road transport, according to the Department of Consumer Affairs.

The rail service, first introduced during a previous price crisis, sends onions from the buffer stock held at Nafed and NCCF warehouses to cities including Delhi, Lucknow, Varanasi, and northeastern destinations like Guwahati, Dibrugarh, and Tinsukia. Consumer Affairs officials have described the initiative as a cost-effective way to move large volumes rapidly — a single rake from Nashik to Delhi costs approximately Rs 35 lakh by rail versus Rs 70 lakh by truck.

"By augmenting market supplies, the objective is to discourage hoarding and speculative trading, improve availability across major consumption centres and keep food inflation under control."

— Government source, as reported by Mint

The Buffer Stock Strategy

The government has set a target to procure 2 lakh tonnes of onions for the state buffer stock under the Price Stabilisation Fund. To attract more supply from farmers, the Centre raised the procurement price by 13 percent on July 4 to Rs 2,125 per quintal, up from Rs 1,875, according to the Department of Consumer Affairs.

A team from the department recently visited Nashik and other key growing states to assess procurement operations and storage conditions. The buffer stocks will be released through multiple channels: wholesale markets, state governments, cooperative agencies, subsidised retail outlets like Safal, and mobile vans selling directly to consumers.

The intervention targets the high-consumption period stretching from Durga Puja through December, when fresh kharif onions are not expected to reach markets until November. Until then, stored rabi onions remain the only supply bridge.

Why Onions Are Politically Explosive

Onion price spikes carry outsized political weight in India. Soaring prices have contributed to electoral defeats in the past, most notably in the 2010 Delhi assembly elections. The current government, with elections behind it, is taking no chances during the festival months.

Onions account for a disproportionate share of vegetable price volatility in India's Consumer Price Index. In September 2024, vegetable inflation contributed 63 percent to overall food price increases, with onion prices surging 66.2 percent year-on-year, according to Mint.

Short crop cycles, storage challenges, and concentrated production in a few states — particularly Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Madhya Pradesh — continue to amplify price swings. The government's multi-pronged approach of buffer procurement, rail logistics, and retail interventions aims to smooth these seasonal spikes, though critics argue structural reforms to India's onion supply chain remain overdue.

What Families Can Expect

With the Kanda Express rolling and buffer stocks entering the market, officials expect retail prices to stabilize in the coming weeks. Subsidised onions are being made available at around Rs 25-35 per kg through government outlets. However, the trajectory will depend on monsoon performance, storage losses, and whether hoarding by middlemen can be curtailed before the festive demand peaks in October and November.

nri_angle: Onion price volatility in India directly affects the cost of essential ingredients for diaspora families who regularly cook Indian cuisine or send remittances to relatives dealing with rising food costs.
